claims.text: Local variations in electronic structure govern the free-energy landscape of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Local magnetic interactions govern the free-energy landscape of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Local chemical ordering and spin states mediate the relevant electronic and magnetic interactions.
The resulting free-energy changes govern the stability of competing ordered and disordered phases.
Local chemical ordering and magnetic spin-state contributions modify local bonding and electronic density.
Changes in composition affect electronic structure and magnetic interaction strengths.
Changes in temperature affect electronic structure and magnetic interaction strengths.
Changes in electronic structure and magnetic interaction strengths alter the free-energy balance between ordered and disordered phases.
Phase stability governed by this mechanism directly affects high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Small compositional deviations from the baseline will systematically shift phase-boundary temperatures.
Small compositional deviations from the baseline will measurably change ordering signatures.
Local ordering will appear or diminish in accordance with the DFT and Monte Carlo forecasts.
The nominal baseline alloy has phase stability and ordering characteristics previously validated by combined simulation and experimental data.
The influence of local electronic and magnetic interactions on phase stability is supported.
